entry_conditions: Peg is closed-grasped and visible; hole, target, peg, TCP, qpos, and qvel are finite. The hole should remain near the demonstrated world workspace. Entry may be early, during insertion, or late in the stable tail.
exit_conditions: Only the unchanged supplied head-x interval, y/z tolerance, minimum axis alignment, and stable held pose define success. Inferred stabilize phase is not a success substitute.
overlap_role: Complete assigned segments are trained. Every [1380,1500) overlap contains high approach/descent, insertion-line settling, and initial +x motion, supplying action supervision across observable phases.
successor_readiness: There is no learned successor. Preserve the closed grasp in the stable tail, while the framework judges readiness only from unchanged task geometry and stability.
failure_signatures: Stage logits conflict with visible geometry; absolute world targets fail to follow a moved hole; descent begins with lateral or angular error; insertion stalls; peg separates from TCP; or IK reports nonconvergence or limits. No stage denotes jam recovery.
continuation_guidance: Use causal observations only. Select this policy for timing ambiguity near the nominal workspace; route materially displaced holes to the hole-frame model and local tracking deviations to the TCP-residual model.
limitations: The stage head predicts deterministic nominal geometry classes, not contact or grasp truth. World targets, collisions, jams, drops, and retry behaviors outside the demonstrations are unsupported.
